h.strategy: Most obvious hypotheses follow a local story: an option matters more when its substitute is missing. These are usually rated likely and often fail. Instead, base hypotheses on robust statistical regularities. (1) Headroom: helpful edits help less in parents that are already strong, for example parents that already contain the strongest option elsewhere. (2) Harmful edits hurt more in strong parents and look harmless in weak parents, because of floor effects. (3) Saturation: adding a second copy of a strong option gives smaller gains than adding the first. (4) Removing an option costs less when the parent has several similar options. Choose conditions that many parents satisfy, so the effect is detectable. Cover several edited fields and both directions. In each 'why', state the obvious prediction and the reason the opposite should hold.

hyps.why: One might expect removing edge 5 to hurt strong parents most, but a 3x3 conv on edge 4 keeps a deep path to the output, so the removal costs less.
One might expect deletion to hurt most in strong parents, but the redundant conv path through edge 5 absorbs the loss of edge 4, making the edit less negative.
One might expect deletion to hurt strong parents most, but node 2 still receives a conv through edge 1, so removing edge 2 costs less.
One might expect pooling to be a uniform mild penalty, but swapping out a 3x3 conv in strong parents causes a large drop, while elsewhere it is nearly neutral.
One might expect pooling to be mildly harmful anywhere, but replacing the key output conv is where the edit costs the most.
One might expect skip to be benign, but swapping out the strongest op on the final edge of a strong parent causes a large drop compared with swapping out weak ops.
One might view deleting an edge as uniformly mildly harmful, but deleting the strongest op from a strong parent hurts far more than deleting a weak op, which is near the floor.
One might expect pooling to be harmful everywhere, but replacing 'none' with pooling adds a path from a low starting point, so the effect is near zero or positive.
One might view skip as a minor change, but replacing 'none' on the direct input-to-output edge adds a residual path, which is worth much more than replacing another op.
One might expect a conv on the shortcut to add capacity, but parents that already feed the output through a conv have little headroom left.
